best_practices.title: Use consistent rule naming convention
best_practices.description: Name rules with pattern: BR_{Action}_{Target}_{Scope}. Example: BR_DerivePayGroup_LATAM. This makes rules easy to find and understand.

best_practices.title: Minimize conditions per rule
best_practices.description: Break complex rules into multiple simpler rules. Each rule should handle one logical derivation. This improves maintainability and debugging.

best_practices.title: Order rules by dependency
best_practices.description: Ensure derived fields that are inputs to other rules execute first. Standard order: onInit -> onChange -> onSave -> validate.

best_practices.title: Always test with edge cases
best_practices.description: Test with: empty fields, null values, employees without company, cross-country scenarios, and new hire vs existing employee scenarios.

best_practices.title: Use onChange for cascading derivations
best_practices.description: When field A derives field B which derives field C, use onChange for real-time cascading so the user sees updates immediately.

best_practices.title: Use validate event for blocking validations
best_practices.description: Use the validate event type (not onSave) when you need to block a save with an error message. This separates validation from derivation logic.

best_practices.title: Document rule purpose and dependencies
best_practices.description: Always add a clear description to each rule. Document which other rules depend on it and what fields it modifies.

best_practices.title: Scope rules by country when possible
best_practices.description: For multi-country implementations, create separate rules per country or country group. This makes maintenance easier and avoids unintended side effects.

best_practices.title: Avoid circular dependencies
best_practices.description: Never create rules where Rule A sets Field X which triggers Rule B which sets Field Y which triggers Rule A. This causes infinite loops.

best_practices.title: Use ELSE branches for completeness
best_practices.description: Always include an ELSE or default branch to handle unexpected values. This prevents fields from being left empty when conditions don't match.
